A roundup of Grist stories, handpicked by our editors. Delivered every Saturday.

Looking Forward

Climate solutions and how to be part of them. Delivered every Friday.

Latest

Latest

  • Michigan just hit pause on a plan to update the controversial Line 5 oil pipeline

    Vivian La

  • The ‘drill, baby, drill’ Democrat who will soon help oversee Texas’ oil industry

    Celeste Guajardo

  • Voters are fed up with for-profit utilities, but they keep rejecting ‘public power’

    Jesse Nichols & Vivian La

  • Nepal hoped for flood aid at COP31. It got nothing.

    Jake Bittle

  • How COP31 became climate diplomacy’s ‘darkest moment’

    Joseph Winters & Jake Bittle

  • The world doesn’t need solar or wind — it needs both

    Matt Simon

Featured

Featured

  • What to know about the Army’s lead detonation in Iowa

    Juanpablo Ramirez-Franco & Brett Chase

  • A walkable city of tomorrow is growing in suburban Utah

    Leia Larsen

  • El Niño is already scrambling your ski season

    Tik Root

Recent

  • How wildfire litigation became big business in America

    Wildfire litigation against utilities has become a fallback strategy to deal with rising losses in a warmer world. But as payouts reach into the billions of dollars, is it sustainable — or just?

    Gloria Dickie, Inside Climate News Wildfires

  • New net-zero community will become Michigan’s first virtual power plant

    The development in Ann Arbor will share its solar and battery power with the grid, as part of a pilot that aims to lower energy costs and provide reliability.

    Alison F. Takemura, Canary Media Cities

  • Data centers’ electricity use is soaring — especially in these states

    In at least four states, hyperscale facilities account for 10 percent or more of the electricity sold.

    Clayton Aldern Energy

  • Is it OK to want a ‘normal life’ during the climate crisis?

    A home, a family, a vacation — therapist Leslie Davenport weighs in on how to reconcile life goals with guilt and fear about climate change.

    Leslie Davenport Culture

The Weekly: A free newsletter from Grist

A weekly roundup of Grist stories, handpicked by our editors and delivered straight to your inbox every Saturday.

Sign Up

Energy

As Texas embraces carbon storage, a Black community questions the risks

Emily Foxhall, The Texas Tribune

  • This surprise cost could derail your heat pump or EV charger installation. Here’s how to avoid it.

    Tik Root

  • As the Colorado River shrinks, calls to drain Lake Powell grow

    Jim Robbins, Yale Environment 360

  • These cranberry bogs come with a side of solar

    Sarah Shemkus, Canary Media

  • Democrats take control of Georgia’s powerful utility regulator

    Emily Jones

Solutions

The affordability election delivered billions for public transit

Benton Graham

  • The cozy radicalism of repair cafés

    Johnny Kauffman

  • 2 years after Mexico relocated their climate-ravaged community, residents struggle to adapt

    Nina Lakhani

  • What to expect as world leaders gather for COP31

    Joseph Winters

  • Electric aviation is taking off in unexpected ways

    Benton Graham

Staff Picks

What’s behind your eye-popping power bill? We broke it down, region by region.

Naveena Sadasivam & Clayton Aldern Energy

  • Chicago has the most lead pipes in the nation. We mapped them all.

    Keerti Gopal, Peter Aldhous, Clayton Aldern, Amy Qin, & Juanpablo Ramirez-Franco

  • First came the wildfire. Then came the scams.

    Naveena Sadasivam

  • Alaska’s $44 billion bet on natural gas

    Lois Parshley

  • A guide to the 4 minerals shaping the world’s energy future

    Jake Bittle

  • In Arizona, a fight against a deadly fungus is under threat from Trump’s health policies

    Zoya Teirstein

A look at the growing ‘disaster economy’ turning crisis into cash

Disasters are big business. We show just how big.

Keep Reading

  • They survived the hurricane. Their insurance company didn’t.

    Zoya Teirstein

  • Trump raised $8 million for Hurricane Helene survivors. Where did it all go?

    Katie Myers

  • Scams are rampant after natural disasters. Here’s how to protect yourself.

    Naveena Sadasivam

  • Two years after a wildfire took everything, Maui homeowners are facing a new threat: Foreclosure

    Anita Hofschneider

  • How to track disaster spending in your community

    Lyndsey Gilpin & Katie Myers

Past extreme weather series

  • State of Emergency

    How climate disasters are reshaping elections.

  • Record High

    Dispatches from the era of extreme heat.

  • Parched

    Life in a drier future.

  • Even the ‘good guys’ of AI are locking in fossil fuels

    Anthropic claims to be developing AI safely. Why doesn’t its own climate impact make the cut?

    Kate Yoder Accountability

  • As black lung disease surges, the Trump administration proposes ‘deregulatory’ protections for miners

    A Biden-era guideline on deadly silica dust has been revised by the Trump administration. Miners' advocates argue it’s a handout to coal companies.

    Katie Myers Health

  • They migrated to New York for work. Now they’re fighting to climate-proof it.

    The worse the weather gets, the more delivery riders work. Can they teach the city how to adapt against climate-fueled disasters?

    Frida Garza & Amir Khafagy Food and Agriculture

  • What Congress’ bill to speed up energy projects would mean for you

    The Senate’s permitting reform bill would make it easier to build renewables — but oil and gas infrastructure, too.

    Austin Corona Energy

Jesse Nichols Science

    Jesse Nichols

  • In the race to find critical minerals, there’s a ‘gold mine’ literally at our shoreline

    Jesse Nichols

  • This enzyme is responsible for life on Earth. It’s a hot mess.

    Jesse Nichols

  • An early-life wildfire exposure sickened these monkeys for decades

    Jesse Nichols

  • In Utah, a ‘hydrocarbon highway’ could run right through this petroglyph-filled canyon

    The Trump administration revived a plan to blast a 5-mile road for trucks carrying crude from oil fields. A new lawsuit aims to block it.

    Leia Larsen Accountability

  • Tribes push back as Congress moves to fast-track energy projects

    A bipartisan “permitting reform” bill would help expand the grid, but tribal nations fear it would mean “the demolition of our heritage.”

    Jake Bittle Indigenous Affairs

  • Nitrates in drinking water are a ‘public health crisis,’ environmentalists warn

    Nearly 120 million Americans are served water with nitrate levels above what public health advocates say is safe. They want the EPA to act.

    Juanpablo Ramirez-Franco Health

  • Carbon dioxide is a climate problem. It might also be a laundry solution.

    A technology born in aerospace uses liquid CO2 to wash clothes without water or a dryer. The challenge is making it work in a home appliance.

    Naoki Nitta Science
